lead: Plateau imposed curfews on three local government areas as killings spread, and the names of the 37 mining suspects who died in Civil Defence custody were published. President Tinubu extended his European vacation and confirmed he would miss the UN General Assembly for a third year, sending Vice President Shettima to New York. The APC won four of five weekend by-elections, the Dangote refinery cut its petrol price by N25 and said it plans a New York listing after expanding, and the APC campaign asked Peter Obi to quit the race over Anambra debts.

items.h: Plateau imposes curfew on three LGAs as killings spread
items.s: The state imposed curfews after at least nine people, five of them bus passengers, were killed in Barkin Ladi, Riyom and nearby communities over the weekend.

items.h: Names of 37 mining suspects who died in custody published
items.s: A civil society coalition released the names and opposed calls to remove NSCDC Commandant-General Ahmed Audi over the deaths in Niger State.

items.h: Tinubu extends vacation and misses UNGA for third year
items.s: Presidential spokesman Bayo Onanuga said the President extended his annual leave in Europe. He will not attend the 81st UN General Assembly, the third year in a row he has stayed away.

items.h: Shettima leads Nigeria's delegation to UN General Assembly
items.s: The Vice President arrived in New York and said Nigeria will be guided by its national interest.

items.h: APC wins four of five by-elections; APM takes one seat
items.s: President Tinubu congratulated the winners of the weekend by-elections in Gombe, Kano, Bauchi and Delta.

items.h: Dangote cuts petrol price by N25 as crude eases
items.s: The refinery lowered its gantry price nine days after raising it.

items.h: Dangote plans NYSE listing after expansion and $10bn power investment
items.s: The refinery plans to list in New York once capacity doubles to 1.4 million barrels a day, and Aliko Dangote said he intends to invest over $10 billion in African power.

items.h: APC campaign tells Obi to quit over Anambra debts
items.s: The APC presidential campaign council demanded Peter Obi's withdrawal over debts it said were incurred while he was Anambra governor.

items.h: Wike tells Obi to forget 2027
items.s: The FCT minister defended his Rainbow Coalition for Tinubu and told Peter Obi to prepare for 2031.

items.h: APC calls Atiku's subsidy plan uncosted
items.s: The APC campaign said the proposed production subsidy lacks a legal and operational framework.

items.h: IGP warns police against bias as ADC demands accountability
items.s: Inspector-General Disu told officers at CARSPO 2026 to stay neutral, and the ADC demanded accountability for attacks on opposition gatherings.

items.h: Troops rescue 23 kidnap victims in Sokoto
items.s: Operation Fansan Yamma foiled several attacks and arrested four suspected terrorists.

items.h: PoS operator arrested over links to bandit leader
items.s: Security operatives in Katsina arrested Isiyaku Nasiru over a financial network tied to Kachalla Muhammadu Filani.

items.h: JAMB allows one-time change of phone numbers and emails
items.s: The board lifted its ban on candidates changing registered SIM numbers and email addresses, subject to verification.

items.h: FG threatens to shut Lagos section of coastal highway
items.s: Officials said the stretch will close within two weeks unless motorists obey safety rules and construction restrictions.

items.h: FDI rises 11.7% but portfolio flows dominate
items.s: Short-term portfolio money made up most foreign capital in the second quarter.

items.h: Cash outside banks rises to N4.87trn
items.s: CBN data showed the first increase in four months.

items.h: Health insurance enrolment passes 23 million
items.s: The NHIA widened cover for cancer, HIV, tuberculosis and maternal care.

items.h: CPPE urges review of permits for foreign traders
items.s: The think tank called for tighter rules on foreign participation in retail trade.

items.h: Dangote Cement hosts London investors before LSE listing
items.s: The company held its capital markets day on 21 September.

items.h: Access Bank repays $500m Eurobond
items.s: The bank redeemed its 2021 five-year bond at maturity.

items.h: Indonesia's Pertamina eyes Nigerian licensing round
items.s: The state oil firm signalled interest in the 2026 round.

items.h: Court postpones El-Rufai's N1bn rights suit
items.s: El-Rufai is challenging the search of his Abuja residence on 19 February.

items.h: Kano says North should not interrupt southern presidency
items.s: Commissioner Ibrahim Waiya also said the state is open to reconciling with Kwankwaso.

items.h: APM to begin zonal town halls in Katsina
items.s: Makinde's campaign will hold meetings across the six zones.

items.h: Lulu explains refusal to sign ex-NFF leaders' paper to FIFA
items.s: Former NFF president Sani Lulu said he disagreed with the position paper.

items.h: Flamingos beat Burkina Faso 2-0
items.s: Nigeria kept a perfect run at the WAFU B U17 Girls Cup in Yamoussoukro.

items.h: Zamfara and XEJet start Abuja-Gusau flights
items.s: The state signed an air route agreement for scheduled services.

items.h: Kwara begins artificial insemination of cattle
items.s: The programme aims to improve breeds and dairy output.

items.h: Local factory starts producing new mosquito nets
items.s: Harvestfield Healthcare began commercial production of next-generation insecticide-treated nets.

items.h: Shettima to open editors' conference in Enugu
items.s: More than 500 editors will discuss democracy and elections.

items.h: AGF's outreach treats 1,500 in Kwara
items.s: Lateef Fagbemi organised free medical and surgical care in Ijagbo.
